title: Uniform torsion cohomology bound for geometric fibres of a proper morphism
statement: Let $p:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $Y$ quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. There exists an integer $c\geq0$ such that for every geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site of $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and every $i>c$, one has $H^i((X_{\bar y})_{\mathrm{et}},F)=0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Torsion means that each local section is killed by some nonzero integer; no common annihilator is assumed. Empty fibres and the empty base are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0A3V, lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension (uniform fibre dimension bound e for finite type over quasi-compact Y); algebra.tex Tag 00P3, lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension (dim X_{\bar y} = dim X_y); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F0V, proposition-cd-affine, globalized by the Zariski-to-etale spectral sequence of literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-prop-sf-cbc/thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd.md (torsion cohomological dimension of a finite-type scheme over a separably closed field is at most 2 dim, giving c = 2e)

proof.text: By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $p$ is of finite type. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound], using the assumed quasi-compactness of $Y$, to choose $e\geq0$ with $\dim X_y\leq e$ for every $y\in Y$. Set $c=2e$. This choice also works when $Y$ is empty, since the asserted bound on its fibres is vacuous.

Fix $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ and let $y$ be its image. By [def-weil-geometric-point] it gives a field extension $\kappa(y)\to\Omega$. By the iterated-base-change identity in [def-pc-base-change], $X_{\bar y}\cong X_y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Both $X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ and $X_{\bar y}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The field-extension clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] therefore gives $\dim X_{\bar y}=\dim X_y\leq e$.

If $X_{\bar y}$ is nonempty, its dimension is an integer $d$ with $0\leq d\leq e$: the bound excludes infinity, and a nonempty space has an irreducible closed subset, so its dimension is not $-\infty$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The algebraically closed field $\Omega$ is separably closed, since every nonconstant separable polynomial is a nonconstant polynomial. Thus [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(\Omega)\leq0$. Apply [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] to the finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $X_{\bar y}$ of dimension $d$: its torsion cohomological dimension is at most $2d$. By [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ has $H^i(X_{\bar y},F)=0$ whenever $i>2e\geq2d$. No constructibility, common annihilator, or invertibility of torsion orders is used.

source.place: Final paragraph, bound 2d+c, specialized to c=0; separably closed field input: sk-lem-base-field-cd/lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd.proof.md

proof.text: If $X_{\bar y}$ is empty, every object of its small etale site is empty and has the empty covering. The sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] forces its group of sections to be the zero group. Thus $F$ is the zero sheaf, and its zero resolution computes zero cohomology in every degree [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Combining this with the nonempty case proves the assertion for $c=2e\geq0$.
